teams.synopsis: One of the best teams in preach history — the only real threat to Ethan's team is Ethan himself.
teams.blurb: Ethan currently has one of the best teams in preach history. <mark class="hl-player">McCaffrey</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Swift</mark> in the backfield, while <mark class="hl-player">AJ Brown</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Devonta Smith</mark> catch the passes. And to top it all off, two respective top-5 players at their position filling out the QB and TE spots. The team is good, and there isn't much to say that can take away from it. The biggest threat to Ethan's downfall isn't anyone in the league — it's himself. Word of advice for the young manager: it gets hot near the sun, don't fly too high.

teams.synopsis: Right behind Ethan, but an argument could be made this is actually the #1 team — CeeDee is unstoppable.
teams.blurb: Carmine is just below Ethan in the power rankings; however, you could make an argument his team could be number 1. <mark class="hl-player">Josh Allen</mark> has been struggling, but the rest of the squad is deep enough to keep the team afloat until he returns to form. A struggling <mark class="hl-player">Pollard</mark> and an injury to <mark class="hl-player">Saquon</mark> could put this team at risk, but <mark class="hl-player">CeeDee Lamb</mark> is arguably the best wide receiver in football today, and seems to be playing angry at literally everyone for no reason.

teams.synopsis: It pains me to rank him this high, but the playoff spot is earned — the RB room still needs an upgrade.
teams.blurb: As much as it pains me to put Brandon this high, he's earned this spot. <mark class="hl-player">Jamarr Chase</mark> is showing everyone why you drafted him where you drafted him, and it's propelling Brandon to a playoff spot. He does rely heavily on his wide receivers, though, as <mark class="hl-player">Aiyuk</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Pittman</mark> are both the next guy up after Chase. A trade should be in the works to bring in a better running back to help even out the squad. Overall, Brandon is primed to make a splash in the playoffs, and he's not someone I want to end up facing in Round 1.

teams.synopsis: A quiet 6-4 climb behind Dak and Etienne — one of the deepest WR rooms in the league to boot.
teams.blurb: Aidan has very quietly scratched his way to a 6-4 record, and this is largely due to the help of <mark class="hl-player">Dak</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Etienne</mark>, who have both been balling in recent weeks. That doesn't mean the rest of his team is bad, either — one of the deepest wide receiver rooms in the league, and to cap it all off, the best tight end in football. Quigley's team is deep and scary, though a tough loss this last week to Brandon will put a damper on his momentum.

teams.synopsis: A slow start turned around — Diggs and Bijan give this team a real shot at a championship.
teams.blurb: After a very slow start to the season, Kelly has found a way to revitalize his team and compete for a fantasy championship this season. This is most likely due to him getting the better of Brandon in a trade, as he does to someone every year. <mark class="hl-player">Stefon Diggs</mark> is showing he can be all you need to win any week, and the combo with <mark class="hl-player">Bijan</mark> is very threatening. A solid team built around these two players can compete with anyone any given Sunday. We all knew the seasoned fantasy manager was gonna figure it out — it was just a question of when.

teams.synopsis: A 6-4 record despite real holes at RB — the receiver room outside of Thielen is thin, but a playoff run is still alive.
teams.blurb: One may look at Baylen's team and ask how he's 6-4. However, that doesn't matter — only record does — but his team is lacking in many places. Pacheco and Rhamondre are not the two backs you want leading you into the playoffs, especially since they're both prone to underperform. And beyond a gem in Adam Thielen, there's no real WR1 to be found, and he's shown he can't be relied upon every week either. This season remains up in the air for There Is No Door Number Four — a playoff run is possible if he plays his cards right.

teams.synopsis: 150 points and a win over a weaker opponent — the sky's the limit with this receiving corps.
teams.blurb: Cole enters this week riding high after dropping 150 points and getting the win over a weaker opponent. It looks like Maney's team may have just figured it all out — the squad is solid and boasts arguably the best receiving corps in the league with <mark class="hl-player">Amon-Ra</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Keenan Allen</mark>. For Maney, the sky is the limit as he lines up against one of the tougher and more passionate teams in the league; a win is necessary.

teams.synopsis: A fringe playoff team now — San Giacomos Frannys Fanny is finding its footing at the right time.
teams.blurb: Charlie Gorman is now a fringe playoff team, and if you told me this before the season started I would have laughed in your face. However, Gorman's team has found its footing and is putting up a fight as we approach the end of the year. At a time when wins are extremely important, having to start AJ Dillon is never a good sign. However, once Kamara returns from bye, San Giacomos Frannys Fanny have a very solid and respectable squad, with a stud in Tyreek Hill. Look for Gorm to make some noise as we approach playoff season.

teams.synopsis: White is breathing new life into a once-forgotten team — a new Raiders staff could finally unlock Adams.
teams.blurb: Deniz's team has been on a downfall recently, and this was capped off by a loss to Gegwich last week. However, the emergence of <mark class="hl-player">Rachaad White</mark> as a running back 1 breathes new life into this once-forgotten team. Deniz is hoping a new Raiders coaching staff will finally get the ball to <mark class="hl-player">Davante Adams</mark> so he can return to his previous all-pro form. However, with the loss of <mark class="hl-player">Deshaun Watson</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Amari Cooper</mark> takes a big hit fantasy-wise. Deniz should be in the market to switch his team around as he hopes to sneak into the playoffs.

teams.synopsis: Gibbs is finally living up to the hype — a DJ Moore revival with Justin Fields back could seal a win.
teams.blurb: Max's team is coming off a fresh win last week against a respectable Gorm team; however, he's now faced with a dog in Gegwich, and the whole league is watching how he'll respond. <mark class="hl-player">Gibbs</mark> is finally being the player we all wanted him to be, and Malich is a happy man because of it. Hopes for a <mark class="hl-player">DJ Moore</mark> revival, due to the return of <mark class="hl-player">Justin Fields</mark> next week, give Malich hope he'll win this week. However, I don't expect this squad to remain the same as the trade deadline approaches — Malich loves to trade.

teams.synopsis: Another year, another injury to a star player — Lamar playing at an MVP level is the season's last hope.
teams.blurb: Andrew always seems to be getting tested as a manager year after year, as it always feels like one of his star players is hurt. Root's team has no true running back 2, and with the underperformance of <mark class="hl-player">Puka Nacua</mark> the past few weeks, he doesn't have a wide receiver 1 either. Don't be surprised if you see a blockbuster trade coming in soon where Root flips the script on his season. The hopes that <mark class="hl-player">Lamar</mark> can play at an MVP level are the foundation for any hopes of playoff contention.

teams.synopsis: Breece Lightning takes another troubling loss — the trade deadline could shake this team up soon.
teams.blurb: Yet another troubling loss is what the fans of Breece Lightning experienced last week, and it only seems to be a sign of what's coming. Kenneth Walker is underperforming, and the Jets offense is so bad that Breece can't be fantasy consistent. However, his reputation precedes him, and who knows what he'll be able to create, especially with the trade deadline coming up. Ryan hopes the return of Justin Jefferson off the IR will revitalize this young team, and with any luck he'll avoid being in the race for last place.

teams.synopsis: A second win, and a slim, slim chance at the playoffs — for now, just avoid last place.
teams.blurb: No surprise to anybody that Gegwich will be in the bottom two spots, yet this time it's a much more positive note, as he's just earned his second win of the season against a very mediocre team led by Deniz. Hopefully he'll take this as a sign and decide to start winning more games, with the slim, slim, slim chance of him making the playoffs. However, he should focus more on not coming in last and having to drive to Ohio.

teams.synopsis: Not far behind Quin at all — Kupp, Jones, and Conner all need to pick it up fast.
teams.blurb: Ben finds himself in last place again; however, the distance between his team and Quin's is not far at all. Hopefully for Ben's sake, <mark class="hl-player">Kupp</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Jones</mark> will pick it up and play to their skill levels, and <mark class="hl-player">Conner</mark> can return from injury and contribute. One may wonder if Ben has the stamina to ride Gegwich out for the rest of the year; one can only wait and watch as these two teams clash it out in a battle of mediocrity.
